external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and puts jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: The background worker process that picks up jobs and performs the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: The queue used by the web application to put jobs for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used for application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The config store from which the web application reads its settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The config store from which the worker reads its settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to
data_flows.description: The user's browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config. Both of those config stores hold the credentials the process needs

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The zone outside the system's network where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier

assumptions.assumption: The web application presents a web interface because the source describes it as a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it a 'Web application'.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a 'background worker process' that picks jobs up from a queue and does the work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: A user's browser talks to the web application 'across the public internet'.
